headline: Intel says it has put more than one million silicon wafers through ASML's newest and most advanced chip-printing machines, a milestone it announced on 7 Sep 2026.
score_reason: Pool score 6 lowered by 2: the event is from 7 Sep 2026, almost four weeks before this edition, and the 2 Oct article date only re-dates older news.
importance_line: It shows Intel is ahead in using the latest chip-printing machines, which matters to its foundry customers and rival chipmakers, but the count mixes test, research and production wafers and does not show how many chips were sold.
summary: Tom's Hardware reports that Intel announced on 7 Sep 2026 that it has processed more than one million 300-millimetre wafers (the round silicon discs chips are made from) on ASML's High-NA EUV machines, less than two and a half years after its first one was assembled. Intel's count includes wafers used for installation, testing and research as well as production, and Tom's Hardware concludes that Intel has now processed more wafers on these machines than the rest of the industry combined.
